types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign nation-state with defined territory and government. Also called nation, state, sovereign country, nation-state. Examples: United States.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Mentions a sovereign nation; matches schema.org Country.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: FoodCategory: A classification of foods based on target consumer, purpose, or processing level. Also called food group, food type, category of food, food classification. Examples: toddler foods, ultraprocessed foods, foods sold for toddlers, ultraprocessed.

chosen_type.label: FoodCategory
chosen_type.definition: A classification grouping of foods based on shared characteristics such as target consumer, purpose, or processing level.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate represents a food classification; mint new type under Thing.

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: MenuItem
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, person, human being. Examples: Erin Hudson, Jane Houlihan, Marissa Burgermaster, Elizabeth Dunford.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are personal names; schema.org Person fits.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

types.embedding_query_text: Institution: An organized establishment, often academic or medical, that provides services or conducts research. Also called hospital, university, research institute, academic institution. Examples: Children’s Hospital Los Angeles, University of Texas at Austin, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

chosen_type.label: Institution
chosen_type.definition: An organized establishment, such as a hospital, university, or research center, that provides services or conducts research.
chosen_type.justification: Mentions span hospitals and universities; no single candidate covers all, so mint new type.

mentions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

candidates.label: Hospital
candidates.comment: A Hospital is a civic structure and medical institution providing patient treatment with specialized medical and nursing staff and equipment. Also called medical center, clinic, healthcare facility. Examples: Mayo Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, a local emergency room.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A collective entity such as a professional society, nonprofit, or industry group. Also called society, association, nonprofit, group. Examples: World Health Organization, American Society for Nutrition, Healthy Babies Bright Futures, American Academy of Pediatrics.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are organizations; schema.org Organization is exact.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: NGO
candidates.comment: An NGO (Non-governmental Organization) is a non-profit organization that operates independently of any government. Also called non-profit organization, charity, civil society organization. Examples: Doctors Without Borders, Amnesty International, local community charity. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category including for-profit entities.

types.embedding_query_text: Policy: A formal rule, guideline, or standard issued by an authority. Also called guideline, standard, regulation, policy document. Examples: WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model.

chosen_type.label: MedicalGuideline
chosen_type.justification: WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model is a policy‑type guideline; matches MedicalGuideline.

mentions: WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model

candidates.label: MedicalGuideline
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a recommendation made by a standard society or consensus statement on how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Also called clinical guideline, practice recommendation, medical protocol. Examples: "AHA/ACC Heart Failure Guideline", "NICE guidelines for diabetes management", "WHO recommendations for vaccination".

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineRecommendation
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that recommends a process as efficacious, supported by sound data. Also called recommended guideline, best practice recommendation, medical advice. Examples: "guideline recommending statins for high cholesterol", "recommendation for early cancer screening". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineContraindication, which warns against a harmful process.

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that specifically designates a process as harmful, supported by sound data. Also called contraindicated guideline, harmful practice warning, medical prohibition. Examples: "guideline against routine antibiotic use for viral infections", "contraindication for specific surgical techniques". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineRecommendation, which suggests an efficacious process.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: Diet
candidates.comment: A creative work outlining a strategy for regulating food intake to achieve a specific health or fitness goal. Also called Eating plan, nutritional regimen, dietary program, meal plan. Examples: The Mediterranean diet, a ketogenic diet, a low-sodium diet, a vegan diet. Distinct from NutritionInformation, which provides factual data about food content.

types.embedding_query_text: Agency: A governmental body with regulatory or administrative authority. Also called government agency, regulatory body, federal agency, public authority. Examples: US Food and Drug Administration, FDA.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: FDA is a government agency; matches GovernmentOrganization.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

types.embedding_query_text: ClassificationSystem: A systematic framework used to categorize items, such as foods, based on defined criteria. Also called taxonomy, categorization system, classification scheme, framework. Examples: NOVA classification system.

chosen_type.label: CategoryCodeSet
chosen_type.justification: NOVA is a classification system; CategoryCodeSet represents a set of category codes.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: SizeSystemEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size systems used for different product categories. Also called sizing standard, measurement system, apparel sizing convention. Examples: 'US', 'UK', 'EU', 'EN-13402', 'Imperial'.

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: WearableSizeSystemEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common sizing systems specific to wearable products. Also called apparel sizing system, clothing size standard, garment measurement standard. Examples: "US size system", "EU size system", "UK size system".

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

types.embedding_query_text: FoodProcessingCategory: A tier within a processing classification system that groups foods by degree of industrial processing. Also called processing tier, processing group, NOVA group, processing level. Examples: Group one, Group two, Group three, Group four.

chosen_type.label: FoodProcessingCategory
chosen_type.definition: A tier within a food processing classification system that groups foods by degree of industrial processing.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate fits a processing tier; mint new type under CategoryCodeSet.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedureType
candidates.comment: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures. Also called procedure category, intervention type, clinical technique. Examples: "DiagnosticProcedure", "TherapeuticProcedure", "SurgicalProcedure".

candidates.label: MenuSection
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a sub-grouping of food or drink items within a menu. Also called menu category, food section, course. Examples: "Appetizers", "Main Courses", "Desserts", "Drinks", "Vegan Options". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A geographic place, such as a city or region. Also called place, city, area, geographic location. Examples: Austin, Texas.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: Mention is a city/region; schema.org Place matches.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

types.embedding_query_text: Count: A numeric quantity representing the amount of items. Also called number, quantity, total, count. Examples: 21 grocery stores, 2,700 products, 2,783 products, 651 products.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are numeric counts; Quantity datatype captures this.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

types.embedding_query_text: FoodProduct: A specific marketed food item intended for consumption. Also called food item, product, food product, consumer food. Examples: fruit pouches, oat bars, mac and cheese bowls, turkey sausages.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct

candidates.comment: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of price components that collectively form the total price of an offered product. Also called price element type, cost breakdown category. Examples: base price, tax, shipping fee, discount.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration

candidates.label: MiddleSchool
candidates.comment: An educational organization that is a civic structure, typically for children aged around 11-14. Also called junior high school, intermediate school, secondary school (early years). Examples: "Springfield Middle School", "Northwood Junior High", "Acme Intermediate". Distinct from HighSchool, which serves older students.

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.
